readings: In `Products`, compute each `production_type_code`'s average `unit_price` (ignoring missing prices). Compute an overall baseline by averaging `unit_price` directly over all individual products (ignoring missing prices), so each product counts once and types with more products weigh more. Proceed only if the baseline exists. Keep the types whose average is above this baseline. Next, take the simple mean of the kept types' averages, and keep only the types whose average is also above that mean. Return one row with three values, each averaged over the remaining types: their type average price, how far their type average is above the overall baseline, and how far it is above the mean of the kept types.
queries:
WITH
baseline AS (
    SELECT AVG(unit_price) AS baseline_price
    FROM Products
),
type_averages AS (
    SELECT production_type_code, AVG(unit_price) AS average_price
    FROM Products
    GROUP BY production_type_code
),
kept_types AS (
    SELECT t.production_type_code, t.average_price
    FROM type_averages AS t
    CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
    WHERE t.average_price > b.baseline_price
),
kept_mean AS (
    SELECT AVG(average_price) AS mean_price
    FROM kept_types
),
remaining_types AS (
    SELECT
        k.average_price,
        k.average_price - b.baseline_price AS above_baseline,
        k.average_price - m.mean_price AS above_kept_mean
    FROM kept_types AS k
    CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
    CROSS JOIN kept_mean AS m
    WHERE k.average_price > m.mean_price
),
result AS (
    SELECT
        AVG(average_price) AS average_type_price,
        AVG(above_baseline) AS average_above_baseline,
        AVG(above_kept_mean) AS average_above_kept_mean
    FROM remaining_types
)
SELECT
    r.average_type_price,
    r.average_above_baseline,
    r.average_above_kept_mean
FROM result AS r
CROSS JOIN baseline AS b
WHERE b.baseline_price IS NOT NULL
